summary:
Amira Hassan is arrival-ward host who treats the new world as a guest she intends to understand. The life that shows in public is anchored at Tea balcony, Arrival Ward. Amira poured a second pot and the balcony that received it belongs to another world. That routine is not a hobby. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Hospitable, sharp, and careful with other people’s stories. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: they turned down a safer life and have not explained why and the person in front of them now resembles that old mistake. If that truth surfaces at Tea balcony, Arrival Ward, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
